info.title: Agents Control API
info.description: Resource-oriented management API under /v1, with administrator-only /v1/admin resources and numbered pagination. Device protocol endpoints under /api/v1 and browser OAuth/SSO redirects remain separate contracts. Frontend types and SDK are generated from this document.

parameters.name: X-CSRF-Token
parameters.description: Required together with same-origin Origin for cookie-authenticated mutations. Bearer clients do not need CSRF.

post.description: Control validates the desired spec automatically: 400 invalid, 403 beyond the role ceiling or policy, 409 name conflict. On success the new effective configuration applies at once; nothing waits for approval.
Exchanges a Device Flow access token for exactly one new Agent. A second exchange of the same authorization returns 409.

registrationToken.description: A Device Flow access token for scope agents:enroll and this instance's registration audience, issued to the agentd client.

kind.description: invalid, unauthorized, forbidden, not_found, conflict, expired, unavailable, internal; data-plane failures may also report origin or capacity.

email.description: Verified email from the last SSO login.

picture.description: HTTPS avatar URL from the last SSO login.

roles.description: Enrollment role ceiling, not the enabled roles.

createdBy.description: The person who registered the device; never used for permission checks.

userId.description: Legacy personal key; new keys always bind a Service Account.

subjectType.description: anonymous and authenticated (every signed-in user) open services and take no subjectId; workspace matches human members only; service_account grants are for egress. See docs/authorization.md.

external.description: A manager authorized sharing beyond the resource Workspace; otherwise a user grant applies only while its subject is a member.

consumer.description: The browser User for serve, the ingress Agent's principal for egress; absent for anonymous serve.

subjectType.description: anonymous and authenticated (every signed-in user) open services and take no subjectId; workspace matches human members only; service_account grants are for egress. See docs/authorization.md.

enabled.description: The role is in the Agent's effective configuration.
The role is in the Agent's effective configuration.

subjectType.description: anonymous and authenticated (every signed-in user) open services and take no subjectId; workspace matches human members only; service_account grants are for egress. See docs/authorization.md.

AgentSpec.description: Server-relevant desired configuration derived from config.yaml. Local paths, listeners, transport details and ingress routes are never uploaded.

EffectiveConfig.description: Desired ∩ role ceiling ∩ Workspace policy, computed automatically by Control. The revision advances only when the content changes; expiresAt bounds offline use by agentd.

ConfigRejection.description: The most recent desired update Control rejected; the previous effective configuration keeps running.

Principal.description: Who an Agent runs as: exactly one User or one Service Account of the Agent's Workspace.

ServiceAccount.description: A machine principal of one Workspace. Revocation is terminal.

UpdateServiceAccount.description: Send either description or status: revoked. The Workspace and name never change.

DeviceAuthorizationInfo.description: The instance's OAuth authorization server and public agentd client for `agentd login`.

DeviceChoice.description: A Workspace the person may register the device in, as themselves (self) or as one of the listed Service Accounts.

userCode.description: The code typed in this browser, for comparison with the terminal.

redirectTo.description: The authorization server URL the browser continues at.

AgentEnrollment.description: The Workspace is a hint that must equal the confirmed authorization's Workspace.

WorkspacePermissions.description: What the caller may do in the Workspace on the control plane. The Console shows actions by it; Control still checks every operation. See docs/authorization.md.

role.description: The caller's Membership role; absent when an instance administrator is not a member.

admin.description: The caller is an instance administrator and holds every permission.
